text:
Gabriel Landeskog came back last season from years of knee trouble and won the Masterton and the Messier awards for it. This season he's simply producing: 8 goals and 13 points in 20 games for the Avalanche, including two in the third-period win in Toronto on November 10 and another in Ottawa two nights later.

Some of it is hot shooting. He's at 26.7%, roughly double what our numbers expect, and his own finishing is 2.3 goals ahead of his chances. Balancing that, his line has been unlucky: Colorado has scored 5.1 fewer goals than the chances deserve with him on the ice. The two roughly cancel, which is why his scoring rate looks sustainable even if the goals slow.

Evan Rawal of the Denver Gazette noted his five-on-five shot volume was way down early, just 13 shots in the first 16 games, then 10 in three. That's the trend to follow. At 14 and a half minutes on a line with Nazem Kadri and Nicolas Roy, he's being used carefully, and it's working.
headline: Landeskog is scoring like he never left
